title: Submission, Deliverables & Handover

scope.purpose: Define how project information becomes a formal submission, an authorized exchange, an accepted deliverable, and a governed handover asset suitable for a stated purpose.
sections: S7.4 LOD / LOI and Permitted Reliance

requirements.statement: Reliance upon information shall require the governed decision and information status applicable to the declared use; Published status alone shall not be treated as evidence that every acceptance, milestone, contractual, professional, or handover decision has occurred.

Submission does not imply authorization, acceptance, milestone approval, handover acceptance, or authorization for reliance; each required decision shall be separately identifiable and recorded through its governed review and authority process.
Every submission shall declare intended use, deliverable scope, LOD/LOI level, target milestone, and the decision event being requested or evidenced where applicable.

Information containers submitted for formal exchange shall pass the governed upstream decision events applicable to that exchange, including internal quality verification, approval for sharing, and coordination review where required; these upstream decisions shall not be represented as downstream authorization or acceptance.
Information shall not be used beyond its declared governed purpose or beyond the reliance authorized by the applicable decision and information status.

Handover deliverables shall include the project-governed record information, asset data, documentation, and operations/maintenance information required by the applicable information requirements and handover instruments; no universal deliverable set shall be inferred solely from this enterprise standard.
Asset data delivered at handover shall conform to governed asset/lifecycle schemas where such schemas are applicable to the project.
All formal exchanges and handover submissions shall be registered and tracked in the project transmittal registry or other governed exchange record defined by the applicable project instruments.

Transmission or technical movement of information shall not by itself constitute formal exchange, approval for sharing, authorization, delivery, acceptance, milestone approval, handover acceptance, or authorization for reliance.

A formal exchange shall intentionally identify the information being issued, its scope, purpose, declared information state, permitted use, relevant milestone or exchange context, traceable issue record, and the governed decision type associated with the exchange where applicable.

Formal exchange shall be platform-independent at the governance level; the selected system or file-transfer mechanism shall not alter the declared purpose, authority, permitted use, required decision type, or acceptance requirements.

Exchanged information shall be decodable by the receiving party from governed declarations sufficient to identify what it represents, why it is being issued, what it may be used for, which decision state it has reached, and material limitations on that use.

A receiving party shall not be expected to infer missing scope, purpose, responsibility, maturity, permitted-use conditions, authorization, acceptance, or authority basis from visual appearance, file format, CDE location, institutional memory, or undocumented assumptions.

Material exchange conditions that change with project phase, responsible party, scope, appointment context, decision type, or authority basis shall be explicitly re-declared before reliance continues under the changed condition.

Handover shall be treated as a governed decision and state-transition event with declared delivered scope, handover-acceptance evidence where required, and transfer of information custody or responsibility as defined by the applicable project instruments; prior authorization or deliverable acceptance shall not by itself constitute handover acceptance.

Where post-handover correction remains after the applicable acceptance decision, the remaining correction scope shall be explicitly bounded and traceable; new scope or changed requirements shall not be treated as defects unless separately governed and agreed.

Acceptance shall be evaluated by the role authorized for the acceptance event against the declared purpose and applicable acceptance criteria; it shall not be inferred from authorization, coordination sign-off, Published status, absolute completeness, visual finality, technical permissions, or workflow execution.

Where authorization for formal exchange is required, the authorization decision shall be recorded separately from receiving-party acceptance and shall identify the authority basis, authorized role, scope, purpose, decision outcome, and supporting evidence.

Where acceptance for a declared use is required, the acceptance decision shall be recorded separately from approval for sharing, coordination sign-off, authorization for formal exchange, milestone approval, and handover acceptance, unless an applicable governing instrument explicitly combines identified decision events and provides the authority basis for doing so.

A CDE state change, transmittal, publication action, workflow completion, technical permission, or tool execution shall not create or expand the authority of the person or system performing that action.

implementation_gaps: Project/enterprise authority mappings for authorize_for_formal_exchange, accept_for_declared_use, milestone_approval and handover_acceptance require reconciliation against governed role definitions and project authority instruments.
Conformance coverage shall be extended to detect collapsed or unsupported decision types and missing authority-basis evidence.
governance_notes: Project deliverable lists, dates, exchange windows, formats, CDE paths, and authority assignments remain project/BEP/RACI declarations unless an applicable enterprise rule explicitly governs them.

Approval for sharing, coordination sign-off, authorization for formal exchange, acceptance for declared use, milestone approval and handover acceptance are distinct TIVERIT decision types. A project instrument may combine events only when the combined event and its authority basis are explicit.

Asset/lifecycle schema governance defines how a schema is identified, versioned, referenced, validated, and deviated from; full client-proprietary or COBie field lists are separate governed artifacts where applicable.
Tool-specific PDF, IFC, NWC, RVT, DWG, or platform export procedures remain in L6 instructions/configuration and do not alter S7 exchange authority or acceptance semantics.

provenance.migration_note: Primary machine-readable L4 S7 source enriched from source doctrine on formal exchange, semantic decodability, acceptance fitness, bounded handover closure, project deliverable/exchange declarations, and asset/lifecycle schema governance. ISO-IMP-005 curator reconciliation further separates approval for sharing, coordination sign-off, authorization, acceptance, milestone approval and handover acceptance without assigning project authority from ISO role names. Project-specific legal, schedule, format, path, schema-instance and appointment effects remain governed by applicable project instruments.
